overview: Use this comparison to select a study scope before selecting a technique. These are choices of study focus, not an official combined curriculum.

products.title: Systematically Attacking The Guard
products.blurb: Compare a broad guard-by-guard course with focused body-lock, over/under and float-passing studies.
products.best_for: You have several passing resources in mind and need to choose one that matches a recurring problem.
products.study_focus: Use this course when a broad guard survey fits your question; choose the narrower linked guides when the passing family is already clear.

fits: You have several passing resources in mind and need to choose one that matches a recurring problem.
consider_alternative_if: If you already know the passing family you want, go directly to its companion guide.

includes: Gordon Ryan: split-squat, half-guard and half-butterfly coverage within a broader course.
Lachlan Giles: body-lock stages and narrated rolling.
Bernardo Faria: over/under entries and troubleshooting; Vagner Rocha: a float volume alongside knee-cut and standing passing.
limits: This comparison covers the linked courses, not every no-gi passing approach; it does not combine their chapter lists into a technical sequence.

start_here.title: Choose breadth or depth from one recurring problem
start_here.task: Describe one recent passing problem without naming a preferred pass. Compare the official outlines: use Ryan’s half-butterfly volume for that guard family, Faria’s troubleshooting volume for an established over/under problem, Giles’s stage description for body-lock progress, or Rocha’s float volume for float-position exits. Select one route and record why its stated starting context matches your problem. Follow the corresponding guide for the first study action.
start_here.section: Comparison anchors: Ryan Volume 4; Faria Volume 2; Giles’s So What’s On This Series description; Rocha Volume 2.
